extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.

faqs.q: What is an MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) used for?
faqs.a: A frac blender mixes proppant, fluid and additives into the slurry that the frac pumpers pump downhole. The MFR-50 is a Mixing and Flow Regulated blender with 50 BBL/min slurry discharge, automatic tub-level regulation and slurry-density control.

faqs.q: What do the MFR variants of the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) cover?
faqs.a: The MFR series offers MFR-10, MFR-15 and MFR-20 for gravel pack, and MFR-50 and MFR-100 for fracturing. This listing is the MFR-50 at 50 BBL/min, so choose the variant from the job rate you need.

faqs.q: How does the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) meter proppant?
faqs.a: It uses calibrated sand screw (auger) metering or a rotating bulk-material metering valve, with inlet and outlet flowmeters. Automatic tub-level regulation and slurry-density control hold the mix steady.

faqs.q: What additive system does the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) include?
faqs.a: It has an integrated Chemical Additive System (CAS) with automatic dosing pumps for liquid and dry additives. That lets the blender dose additives to the slurry rate without manual adjustment.

faqs.q: How does the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) connect to the rest of the fleet?
faqs.a: It can run standalone or connect by wire or wifi to the frac data van, so one operator can see and control it with the rest of the fleet. See the [frac data van](/p/frac-data-van-trailer-mounted-multi-screen-fleet-control-hvac-pantry) for fleet control and recording.

faqs.q: What truck chassis and engines can the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) use?
faqs.a: Chassis options include MAN, Mercedes, Scania, DAF, Volvo, Renault, Tatra, MAZ, MAZ-MAN, Kamaz, NZKT, Kenworth and Peterbilt, and engines include CAT, Mercedes, Deutz, MTU, Detroit Diesel and Volvo Penta. State your preference on the RFQ.

faqs.q: How does the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) differ from a hydration unit?
faqs.a: The blender adds proppant and additives and discharges slurry to the pumpers, while the [hydration unit](/p/frac-hydration-unit-200-bbl-12-12-centrifugal-90-bbl-min-ss316-tote-tanks) prepares the gel beforehand. They run in sequence in a frac fleet.

faqs.q: Where is the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) used?
faqs.a: It is used in hydraulic fracturing fleets for slurry preparation ahead of the frac pumpers. See the guide on [frac and stimulation equipment](/blog/frac-and-stimulation-equipment) and the [frac pumpers](/c/frac-pumpers) it feeds.

faqs.q: What should I send for a frac blender quotation?
faqs.a: Send the slurry rate, proppant metering type, additive requirements, truck chassis and engine preference, the certification needed and the data-van connection. The unit is configured to your specification.

faqs.q: What are the sizes of the blender range for the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min)?
faqs.a: The range runs from MFR-10 to MFR-100, with the 50 BBL/min MFR-50 as this listing. Larger rates use the MFR-100 for fracturing.

faqs.q: How is the frac blender controlled?
faqs.a: Control is local or through the frac data van, which receives readings by wire or wifi. The blender has automatic tub-level regulation and density control, with inlet and outlet flowmeters.

faqs.q: Does Indus stock the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min)?
faqs.a: Yes. We list the MFR-50 frac blender (50 BBL/min) as ex-stock from our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Chassis and engine are quoted to your specification. Send your configuration and destination through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.
